title: Agent bridges, skill and opum-ward plugin packaging
description: Spec §11.2-11.3 and §12. Move the skill draft to skills/ward/SKILL.md, ship .claude-plugin/plugin.json per the peer pattern, `ward agents --check/--update-instructions` for claude and codex. Marketplace entry waits for a release artifact.

acceptanceCriteria.text: T24: Claude and Codex discover guidance and perform check/run on synthetic data without requesting values or self-approving
T25: skill, plugin and CLI release references agree; the marketplace patch validates against the index but is not published before the artifact exists

plan: 1. Land the mechanically specified half: the plugin.json and package.json version agreement as a test, and ward agents --check / --update-instructions --target claude|codex over the managed block spec 11.2 defines.

2. Do not implement the skill-file half of spec 8s row: how a local skill file is explicitly selected decides a tracked document (a flag, a key in .ward/project.json, or host-plugin detection), so it goes to the orchestrator as a design question with a recommendation rather than being invented here.
3. Record what remains for T24 and T25 - the Codex half of the agent contract, and the marketplace entry opum-fleet is holding - and report them with the evidence that exists.
implementationNotes: Plugin name ruled opum-ward by the orchestrator on 2026-09-28 (WCLI-3 Q3); binding once opum-doc records it, with the same record id as the WCLI-3 ADRs. The skill is authored in ward-cli (skills/ward/SKILL.md). The opum-marketplace entry waits for a release artifact (spec §11.3).

SCOPE NOTE from WCLI-50, 2026-09-29, recorded so these files are extended rather than re-created. WCLI-50 landed the minimum of this task's packaging that its own eval gate needs:

- skills/ward/SKILL.md now exists (git mv from the repository root SKILL.md, hardened; WCLI-50 owns the content).
- .claude-plugin/plugin.json now exists (name opum-ward per the WCLI-3 Q3 ruling, version 0.0.0 matching package.json, peer-pattern fields, claude plugin validate clean).

WHY IT COULD NOT WAIT: claude plugin eval loads the plugin from a path, and opum-fleet check-evals.mjs fails any suite whose case names do not start with a directory under skills/ - so WCLI-50's structural check and its run both require the plugin skeleton to exist.

WHAT REMAINS WCLI-14's: the CLI-side bridge work (ward agents --check and --update-instructions, claude and codex targets), release-time versioning of the manifest (0.0.0 is a placeholder that should track the CLI version per the lore-cli pattern), T24, and the marketplace entry with T25. The eval suite under evals/ and scripts/run-eval.sh are WCLI-50's and are not part of this task.

LANDED 2026-09-29 (this pull request), the mechanically specified half of the task.

1. ward agents --check / --update-instructions --target claude|codex (spec section 8's two rows). It reuses the managed block module spec section 11.2 already defines - the same upsert the writer uses - over the project-files port, so the marker grammar, the conflict on malformed markers and the containment refusal of a link out of the checkout are the existing ones rather than a second implementation. New files: src/application/agents.ts, test/agents.test.ts; new codes agent_form_invalid, agent_target_unknown and agent_option_unexpected, named in the family the neighbouring usage errors use.

EXIT SEMANTICS ARE TAKEN FROM THE PEER, NOT INVENTED, and the reason is recorded because it is the one place a reader may expect the stricter shape: absence is REPORTED and does not fail (exit 0), stale and malformed always fail (exit 6), and --require-installed makes absence fail too. That is quest agents' documented contract, and ward-cli's own non-disclosure contract test requires every example of a command that does not unlock the vault to exit 0 in this repository's checkout, which has no Ward bridge. The check reports malformed as a STATE (like ward doctor's instructions check) rather than raising, while the writer raises the existing instructions_markers_conflict - a check answers about a repository, a writer refuses a write.

2. The plugin.json and package.json version agreement is now a test (test/plugin-manifest.test.ts), which is the peer pattern that exists because it was paid for: lore-cli added exactly this check after 0.4.3 shipped carrying 0.4.2, and quest-cli's runbook says plainly that nothing compares its plugin.json to package.json, "which is exactly why it drifted silently". The same file pins the plugin name (opum-ward), the repository reference, and that the packaged skill is the frontmattered one under skills/ward/.

MUTATION PROOF for the contract test that now covers the new command: with a line added to agentsCommand reading the default ~/.ward, the non-disclosure example run goes red (exit 1 against the planted unreadable trap); with it removed, green. Both halves measured, mutation reverted.

DELIBERATELY NOT LANDED, and it is the design question: the skill-file half of spec section 8's row ("and selected local skill files"). Spec section 11.2 wants a local skill at .claude/skills/ward/SKILL.md for Claude and .agents/skills/ward/SKILL.md for Codex, explicitly selected, and warns against a duplicate when the marketplace plugin already supplies the skill. Both peer CLIs express the selection as an agents.skill_source value in their own workspace config (repo|plugin|none, default repo); Ward has no equivalent config, and adding a key to .ward/project.json changes a tracked document's schema. Sent to the orchestrator with the evidence rather than decided here.
